translations.t0000: The Parking Ascona Lido records an exit on 13 October at 16:02 CEST; Vogel's card was also charged on 13 October at 16:02 (UTC 14:02). The expense report states return on 13 October. This is consistent with a Monday-afternoon drive home and arrival at approximately 19:00.
translations.t0001: Vogel claims to have been absent from the office for the entire long weekend (Friday evening through Monday afternoon).
translations.t0002: There is no camera footage on the engineering floor, no usable badge data, and no audit logs for the period in question. Neither presence nor absence in the office can be positively established for Friday night. June Okada's statement places the vehicle in the car park as late as shortly before 21:00, which contradicts an absence from 18:00 onwards, but does not prove that Vogel spent the night in the office.
translations.t0003: Vogel had access to Slide 11 (Real/Decoy mapping) while formatting the Q1 board deck, before the slide was removed on instruction. The undocumented current staging path (K2) is, according to statements by Andrin Caduff and Lukas Hofer, known only to individuals who have been with the company since before 2023 and worked directly with the checkpoints — Vogel does not meet this criterion. Lukas Hofer explicitly confirms that the diligence documents did not reveal the staging path. The decompression behaviour (K3) is, according to Hofer's statement, unknown even to many engineers. The logging window (K4) was known to approximately 40 people. Knowledge combination: Vogel may have had K1 (Real/Decoy) through Slide 11 and K4 (logging window) through general availability — but K2 (staging path) is not established and has been explicitly denied by two key witnesses.
translations.t0004: Vogel had no documented direct access to the engineering floor or the scratch volumes as a normal part of her work. The data-room export role dr-export-ro theoretically had read access to staging trees (SEC-419), but the exfiltration was carried out physically from a local workstation console — this access path was not the one used. Physical access would have been possible via the propped alley door (K6), but that applies to anyone.
translations.t0005: Vogel's alibi for the night of the offence (23:10 CEST Friday to 05:58 CEST Saturday) is unconfirmed and contains active contradictions: (1) June Okada's witness statement places Vogel's vehicle in the car park shortly before 21:00, later than Vogel's claimed departure at around 18:00; (2) a card payment on 11 October at 07:52 CEST in St. Gallen contradicts a continuous presence in Ascona. The Parking Ascona Lido receipt records entry on Saturday (without an exact time) and exit on Monday — consistent with an arrival on Saturday morning after the offence. The geographical sequence (St. Gallen 07:52, San Bernardino 09:54, Ascona parking from Saturday) is compatible with a departure following the night of the offence.
translations.t0006: According to June Okada's witness statement, Vogel's vehicle was still in the car park shortly before 21:00 — significantly later than Vogel's claimed departure at around 18:00. This is not direct proof of guilt, but it undermines the credibility of the stated departure time.
translations.t0007: A card payment at 07:52 CEST on 11 October in St. Gallen disproves the claim of having been in Ascona for the entire Friday night. Combined with the vehicle remaining in the car park until approximately 21:00, a time gap emerges: during the night of the offence (23:10–05:58 CEST) Vogel was possibly in or near St. Gallen.
translations.t0008: Slide 11 contained the Real/Decoy path mapping; Vogel had access while formatting. The undocumented staging path (K2) is, according to Lukas Hofer's statement, not contained in the diligence materials — however, Slide 11 may have contained a path reference. This has not been forensically excluded.
translations.t0009: Vogel's technical self-portrait ('I have June reset my password', 'I once escalated to Lukas because a spreadsheet wouldn't sort') is a statement, not evidence. The exfiltration required operational knowledge, but no exceptional technical expertise — operating a bulk-copy command and deleting a snapshot are actions a non-technical person could carry out with prior guidance or instruction.
translations.t0010: The Parking Ascona Lido record and the expense report establish Vogel's presence in Ascona from (at the latest) Saturday 11 October, but not for Friday night. The card payment at 07:52 CEST in St. Gallen on Saturday morning and the vehicle in the car park shortly before 21:00 on Friday evening contradict the claimed early departure and overnight presence in Ascona. Vogel's alibi for the offence window (23:10–05:58 CEST) is actively disproved, not merely unsubstantiated. The absence of staging-path knowledge (K2) is the strongest exculpatory argument, but it rests on witness statements and is not forensically established. The case file remains open.
translations.t0011: Renata Vogel's alibi for the night of the offence is unconfirmed: according to a witness statement her vehicle was still in the office car park shortly before 21:00, and a card payment in St. Gallen in the early hours of Saturday contradicts the claim of having been in Ascona the entire night. The strongest exculpatory argument — that she was unaware of the undocumented staging path and that the diligence materials did not reveal it — rests on witness statements but has not yet been forensically refuted.
translations.t0012: The garage log contains no exit record for SG 482 117 on 10 October in the provided extract — it is unclear when the vehicle left the car park; this is the central unresolved time point.
translations.t0013: June Okada's vehicle identification ('green Volvo estate with roof box') is based on type and colour, not on the licence plate — it could be a different vehicle, although Vogel's parking permit corresponds exactly to this type.
translations.t0014: The card payment at 07:52 CEST on 11 October in St. Gallen could theoretically have been made by another person using Vogel's card — there is no evidence for this.
translations.t0015: The Parking Ascona Lido receipt does not state an entry time on 11 October; it is unclear whether Vogel arrived early or late on Saturday.
translations.t0016: Whether Slide 11 contained the full staging path or only a description of the artefacts cannot be reconstructed from the case files; Lukas Hofer's statement relates to the diligence materials, not to Slide 11 itself.
translations.t0017: The decompression knowledge (K3) is, according to Hofer's statement, unknown even to many engineers — whether Vogel could have acquired it through other channels (e.g. Jira ticket SEC-486, which she created herself) remains open. SEC-486 is titled 'Improve error message on decompress-on-write overflow' and was created by Vogel as reporter, which suggests some awareness of the phenomenon.
translations.t0018: Contacts between Vogel and Kestrel after the deal collapsed (beyond known channels) have not been excluded.
translations.t0019: Favre claims he travelled to Val Müstair by train and PostBus on Thursday evening. Are there rail/bus tickets, card payments, or other records to substantiate this journey?
translations.t0020: Card payments by Favre during the period in question (10–13 October) could physically establish his presence outside St. Gallen.
translations.t0021: The garage log (with the known clock offset of +1h) could show whether Favre's vehicle — if he has one — was at the scene. He states he does not own a car.
translations.t0022: Favre claims to have spent four hours on a video call with Lukas Hofer on Saturday 11 October working on an incident. Slack logs and the incident channel with timestamps could confirm this.
translations.t0023: Are there witness statements or further evidence (photos, messages) from the girlfriend or her family confirming Favre's presence in Val Müstair?
translations.t0024: Favre borrowed two 18-TB arrays and claims they were in the Glattbrugg colo the entire time. A colo intake receipt and their return with intact seals are crucial to ruling out a connection with the device used in the offence.
translations.t0025: Favre created the Confluence page 'Storage Integrity Controls (WIP)' containing the Real/Decoy mapping and set standard permissions (eng-all), thereby making knowledge of the real artefacts available to 9 accounts (16 views).
translations.t0026: Publishing the page was a documented good-faith error that Favre acknowledged immediately. He did not share it covertly; he used the standard engineering-space permissions model. Iris Ammann confirmed that the documentation itself was correct — only the permissions were wrong. Furthermore, this page increased the pool of knowledgeable individuals to 9 accounts, which broadens rather than narrows the pool of suspects.
translations.t0027: Favre admitted the error immediately after the ticket was opened and described it as a good-faith mistake.
translations.t0028: Iris Ammann confirms that the documentation was correct; only the permissions were wrong.
translations.t0029: Favre shared the page publicly in the Slack channel #eng-infra — transparent conduct, not concealment.
translations.t0030: The broad accessibility is real and has widened the pool of suspects; the error cannot be undone.
translations.t0031: Knowledge of the scratch volumes and their lack of audit linkage is specific but also known to others (Lukas Hofer, Chiara Bernasconi, potentially all Confluence readers). Knowledge alone does not establish suspicion as long as no presence at the scene is established.
translations.t0032: Lukas Hofer independently confirms that scratch volumes are generally used for bulk copies and that the absence of auditing is known.
translations.t0033: Favre actively distances himself from the scratch incident and refers to his whereabouts.
translations.t0034: The moonlighting is a breach of contract, but the company (a scheduling app for dog groomers) is demonstrably not relevant to industrial espionage. Favre disclosed it unprompted, which argues against calculated criminal intent. CHF 400/week is a weak financial motive relative to the risk of prosecution.
translations.t0035: Favre describes the secondary employment as entirely irrelevant to industrial espionage and disclosed it proactively.
translations.t0036: The breach of contract is real and established; the harmless nature of the company is Favre's assertion only, not independently verified.
translations.t0037: Favre claims to have travelled to Val Müstair by train and PostBus on the evening of Thursday 9 October (last PostBus at 18:00); no personal vehicle.
translations.t0038: The calendar (OOO from 18:00 CEST on 9 October) and the automatic out-of-office reply (18:05 on 9 October) are consistent with a departure on Thursday evening. Lukas Hofer implicitly cites Thursday '22:00' as the daily limit (departure from St. Gallen) as known. There are no rail or PostBus tickets and no card payments for the journey itself in the case files. No garage-log entry for a vehicle belonging to Favre (he states he has no car; no licence plate is registered in the files). The permit-list export is contained in the files, but no vehicle belonging to Favre appears in it. The consistency of multiple independent sources (calendar UTC, auto-reply, Slack message, Saturday incident response) supports the claim without fully proving it.
translations.t0039: Favre claims to have been in Val Müstair all day on Saturday 11 October and to have spent four hours on a video call with Lukas Hofer working on incident INC-0412.
translations.t0040: Four independent timestamped Slack messages establish Favre's presence in Val Müstair on Saturday 11 October: (1) 13:02 CEST Lukas Hofer asks whether Yannick is reachable, (2) 13:09 CEST Favre checks in from Val Müstair with screen share, (3) 13:11 CEST Favre writes in the #incidents channel that he is in Val Müstair without a car, (4) 17:48 CEST Lukas Hofer thanks Yannick at the close of the incident. Lukas Hofer independently confirms in interview that Favre was on the call with him for four hours. The incident channel ran on a separate, continuously active logging system. This time window (13:01–17:48 CEST) does not overlap with the offence window (23:10 Fri – 05:58 Sat), but it does physically establish Favre's absence from St. Gallen as late as Saturday midday, making a return journey before the start of the offence (23:10 CEST Friday) extremely unlikely.
translations.t0041: Favre claims the two borrowed 18-TB portable arrays were in the Glattbrugg colo for the entire period in question and never came to St. Gallen.
translations.t0042: Helpdesk ticket HD-3999 documents the loan (seals 44817 and 44818, courier to Glattbrugg on 9 October). June Okada confirms by email dated 14 October that both arrays were returned on Monday 13 October at 18:20 with intact seals. Favre himself reported the return on 14 October at 09:12 CEST via Slack. Additionally, an expense report from Priya Raghunathan establishes that she personally drove to the Glattbrugg colo on 9 October ('Drove to the Glattbrugg colo Thu 9 Oct to hand over migration checklists'), corroborating the delivery to the colo site. The arrays are excluded as the device used in the offence.
translations.t0043: Favre states he does not own a car; no vehicle appears in the garage log or parking-permit register.
translations.t0044: The garage barrier log had not yet been fully analysed at the time of this analysis (received 01.12. per notebook NB-L72). The permit list was transmitted on 26 November, but no entry explicitly confirms that Favre has no registered vehicle. The claim is plausible and consistent with the Val Müstair journey by public transport, but remains formally unsubstantiated pending full garage-log analysis.
translations.t0045: All three categories of perpetrator knowledge (Real/Decoy mapping, current staging path, decompression behaviour) were available to Favre: he created the Confluence page containing the mapping, has known the staging path since before 2023, and as the infrastructure engineer assigned to ticket ML-975 (checkpoint compression) the decompression behaviour is within his professional knowledge. This knowledge is not, however, exclusive to Favre: Lukas Hofer, Andrin Caduff, Iris Ammann and the 9 Confluence readers share it in various combinations.
translations.t0046: Favre had technical access to scratch-02 (he built the arrays). Physical access to the engineering floor is possible via the propped alley door without a badge. No vehicle is registered in the system; no card transaction in St. Gallen during the offence window. Val Müstair is approximately 4 hours from St. Gallen; without a car and with the last PostBus at 18:00 on the day before the offence, an undetected round trip during the night of the offence is practically excluded, though not forensically impossible.
translations.t0047: The offence window runs from 23:10 CEST Friday to 05:58 CEST Saturday. According to independently confirmed Slack logs, Favre was reachable in Val Müstair from 13:09 CEST on Saturday and was actively involved in the incident. There is no evidence of his presence in St. Gallen during the offence window. A return journey on Friday evening, commission of the offence overnight, and a return to Val Müstair before 13:09 Saturday would be logistically extremely unlikely (4h+ one way, no car, no public transport available), but cannot be formally excluded in the absence of complete public-transport ticket data.
translations.t0048: The garage log (received 01.12., not yet fully analysed) could theoretically show a vehicle that can be linked to Favre.
translations.t0049: There are no rail or PostBus tickets in the case file that physically document the outward journey on 9 October or the return journey on 13 October — only Favre's own statement and consistent supporting evidence.
translations.t0050: The identity and connections of the Winterthur moonlighting company have not been independently verified.
translations.t0051: The strongest exculpatory point is Favre's presence in Val Müstair on Saturday 11 October (13:01–17:48 CEST), independently confirmed by multiple timestamped Slack messages and Lukas Hofer's interview. Combined with the logistical near-impossibility of an unobserved round trip without a car (4h+ one way, last PostBus at 18:00 the day before) and the complete absence of any location data (card, vehicle) placing Favre in St. Gallen during the offence window, this constitutes a strong but not fully forensically closed exculpatory position. Deductions for: incomplete garage-log analysis, absent public-transport ticket data, unverified moonlighting company.
translations.t0052: Yannick Favre's presence in Val Müstair on the Saturday of the offence is established by independent, timestamped Slack logs and a witness confirmation (Lukas Hofer); a return journey to St. Gallen, commission of the offence, and a further return before 13:09 would be logistically impracticable without a car or public transport. The notable points (Confluence error, scratch knowledge, moonlighting) have harmless, substantiated, or proactively admitted explanations; no positive evidence links Favre to the scene.
translations.t0053: The garage log (received 01.12., not yet analysed) could theoretically show a vehicle attributable to Favre.
translations.t0054: No rail or PostBus tickets are in the case file to physically document the journey to and from Val Müstair.
translations.t0055: The identity and connections of the Winterthur moonlighting company have not been independently verified.
translations.t0056: The 81 minutes of interview transcript (IV04-L45: 'recording continues, 81 minutes removed') are not in the case file; content unknown.
translations.t0057: Whether Favre could theoretically have departed on Friday evening before the last PostBus and returned early on Saturday is logistically extremely unlikely but cannot be formally excluded without public-transport data.
